about: Weekly schedule from the Come, Follow Me manual's numbering. Overviews, concepts and questions are written for Scripture Study Links in its own words. Read the Church's lesson for the full manual.

weeks.title: I Will Turn Their Mourning into Joy
weeks.label: Jeremiah 31-33; Jeremiah 36-38; Lamentations 1; Lamentations 3

weeks.title: A New Spirit Will I Put within You
weeks.label: Ezekiel 1-3; Ezekiel 33-34; Ezekiel 36-37; Ezekiel 47

weeks.title: There Is No Other God That Can Deliver
weeks.label: Daniel 1-7

weeks.title: I Will Love Them Freely
weeks.label: Hosea 1-6; Hosea 10-14; Joel 1-3
weeks.overview: Hosea's own marriage becomes a living parable: the Lord keeps loving a covenant people who keep wandering, and He promises to bring them home. Joel adds a call to return with the whole heart and a promise that the Spirit will be poured out on everyone.

concepts.title: A covenant love that does not give up
concepts.text: Hosea is told to keep loving a wife who leaves him. The story shows how the Lord feels about Israel: hurt by betrayal, yet still reaching out.
concepts.ponder: Where have I felt the Lord keep reaching for me after I wandered?

concepts.title: Mercy more than ritual
concepts.text: The Lord wants steady love and real knowledge of Him, not just offerings. Jesus quoted this line twice in Matthew.
concepts.ponder: Which of my religious habits are drawing me closer to God, and which have become routine?

concepts.title: I will love them freely
concepts.text: The book ends with an invitation to come back, and the Lord's promise to heal and love His people freely.
concepts.ponder: What would it look like to accept His love as a gift rather than something earned?

concepts.title: Rend your heart, not your garments
concepts.text: Joel asks for repentance on the inside, not just outward signs of mourning, and promises the Lord will restore what the locusts ate.
concepts.ponder: What has the locust eaten in my life that the Lord could restore?

concepts.title: The Spirit on all flesh
concepts.text: Joel foresees a day when sons, daughters, old and young all receive the Spirit. Peter quoted it at Pentecost, and Moroni quoted it to Joseph Smith.
concepts.ponder: How is this prophecy being fulfilled in the people I know?

weeks.title: Seek the Lord, and Ye Shall Live
weeks.label: Amos 1-9; Jonah 1-4; Obadiah
weeks.overview: Three prophets, three angles on one invitation. Amos tells a comfortable, wealthy Israel that worship without justice is empty and that the way to life is to seek the Lord. Obadiah warns Edom that pride and betraying a brother lead to a fall, and looks ahead to saviours on Mount Zion. Jonah runs from his call, is rescued anyway, and learns that God's mercy reaches even Israel's enemies.

concepts.title: Seek the Lord and live
concepts.text: Amos's central invitation: not more ceremonies at Bethel or Gilgal, but turning to the Lord Himself. Seeking Him means loving good, hating evil and letting fairness flow like a river.
concepts.ponder: What does seeking the Lord look like in my ordinary week?

concepts.title: The Lord reveals His plans to His prophets
concepts.text: Amos says the Lord does nothing without first revealing His purposes to His servants the prophets. A lion has roared; a prophet cannot stay silent.
concepts.ponder: How do I listen for what the Lord is revealing through living prophets?

concepts.title: A famine of hearing the word
concepts.text: The worst famine Amos describes is not of bread but of hearing the Lord's words, with people searching everywhere and not finding them.
concepts.ponder: How do I keep from drifting into a spiritual famine?

concepts.title: Worship that cares for the poor
concepts.text: Israel sold the needy for a pair of shoes, cheated with false scales and still held feasts. Amos says the Lord will not accept worship that ignores the oppressed.
concepts.ponder: Is there anyone my comfort keeps me from noticing?

concepts.title: The Lord will rebuild and restore
concepts.text: After the warnings, Amos ends with hope: the fallen house of David raised up, the land rebuilt and Israel planted never to be uprooted again.
concepts.ponder: Where do I need to trust that the Lord rebuilds what is broken?

concepts.title: Pride and betraying a brother
concepts.text: Edom felt safe in its high rock cities and stood by, even helped, when Jerusalem fell. Obadiah says pride deceives, and how we treat a brother comes back on us.
concepts.ponder: Have I stood aside when someone close to me needed help?

concepts.title: Saviours on Mount Zion
concepts.text: Obadiah ends with deliverers on Mount Zion and the kingdom belonging to the Lord. Latter-day Saints often connect this line with serving others in temples.
concepts.ponder: How can I be a saviour on Mount Zion for someone?

concepts.title: You cannot outrun the Lord, and He gives second chances
concepts.text: Jonah runs the opposite way, yet the Lord follows him into the storm and the sea, hears his prayer from the fish and sends him a second time.
concepts.ponder: Where is the Lord giving me a second chance right now?

concepts.title: God's mercy reaches everyone, even enemies
concepts.text: Nineveh repents and is spared, and Jonah is angry. The book ends with God's question about caring for a great city full of people and animals, and leaves the answer to the reader.
concepts.ponder: Whom do I find it hard to want God to forgive?

concepts.title: The sign of Jonah
concepts.text: Jonah's three days in the fish became a sign Jesus pointed to for His own death and resurrection.
concepts.ponder: What does Jonah's rescue teach me about the Savior's power over death?

weeks.title: He Delighteth in Mercy
weeks.label: Micah 1-7; Nahum 1; Habakkuk 1-3; Zephaniah 1-3
weeks.overview: Micah condenses true religion into one line: do justly, love mercy, walk humbly with God, and he names Bethlehem as the birthplace of a coming ruler. Nahum, Habakkuk and Zephaniah wrestle with judgment and evil, and each lands on trust: the Lord is good, the just live by faith, and the Lord rejoices over His people with singing.

concepts.title: What the Lord requires
concepts.text: Not thousands of rams or rivers of oil, but to do justly, love mercy and walk humbly with God.
concepts.ponder: Which of the three is the Lord inviting me to work on now?

concepts.title: Out of Bethlehem
concepts.text: Micah names little Bethlehem as the place a ruler would come from, one whose goings forth are from of old. Matthew quotes it in the Christmas story.
concepts.ponder: How does knowing the Savior was foretold strengthen my faith in Him?

concepts.title: The mountain of the Lord's house
concepts.text: In the last days people will stream to the Lord's house to learn His ways, and weapons will become farm tools. Isaiah 2 has nearly the same words.
concepts.ponder: What do I go to the Lord's house to learn?

concepts.title: He delights in mercy
concepts.text: Micah closes by marveling at a God who pardons, does not stay angry, and throws our sins into the depths of the sea.
concepts.ponder: What sin do I keep fishing back out that He has already cast into the sea?

concepts.title: The Lord is good, a stronghold
concepts.text: Even in a book about Nineveh's fall, Nahum pauses to say the Lord is good and knows those who trust Him.
concepts.ponder: When has the Lord been a stronghold for me in a day of trouble?

concepts.title: Wait for it: the just shall live by faith
concepts.text: Habakkuk asks why evil seems to win. The Lord tells him to write the vision plainly and wait, because the just live by their faithfulness. Paul built on this line.
concepts.ponder: What question am I waiting on the Lord to answer?

concepts.title: Rejoice even when the fig tree fails
concepts.text: Habakkuk ends choosing joy in the Lord even if every crop fails, because the Lord is his strength.
concepts.ponder: Can I name a reason to rejoice in the Lord on a hard day?

concepts.title: The Lord rejoices over you with singing
concepts.text: Zephaniah moves from the day of the Lord to a tender ending: a pure language restored and the Lord Himself joyful over His people.
concepts.ponder: How does it change things to picture the Lord rejoicing over me?

weeks.title: Holiness unto the Lord
weeks.label: Haggai 1-2; Zechariah 1-4; Zechariah 7-14
weeks.overview: The exiles are home, but the temple sits unfinished while people build their own houses. Haggai tells them to put the Lord's house first. Zechariah encourages them with visions, teaches that the work goes forward by the Spirit, and looks ahead to a humble King on a donkey, a pierced Savior, and a day when even cooking pots are holy to the Lord.

concepts.title: Consider your ways: the Lord's house first
concepts.text: The people earn wages that seem to fall into a bag with holes. Haggai ties their struggle to leaving the Lord's house in ruins.
concepts.ponder: What would putting the Lord's house first look like for me this week?

concepts.title: The glory of the latter house
concepts.text: Builders who remembered Solomon's temple felt this one was small. The Lord promises its glory will be greater and brings peace there.
concepts.ponder: When have small beginnings in my life turned out to matter most?

concepts.title: Turn to me, and I will turn to you
concepts.text: Zechariah opens with a short, generous promise from the Lord of hosts.
concepts.ponder: What first step of turning could I take today?

concepts.title: Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit
concepts.text: Zerubbabel's great task will be finished not by strength but by the Lord's Spirit. Do not despise the day of small things.
concepts.ponder: What am I trying to do by my own power that needs His Spirit?

concepts.title: Fasting that shows mercy
concepts.text: The Lord asks whether their fasts were really for Him, then names what He wants: true judgment, kindness and protecting the widow, orphan, stranger and poor.
concepts.ponder: How could my next fast bless someone in need?

concepts.title: Your King comes, lowly, on a donkey
concepts.text: Zechariah pictures a King who brings salvation humbly. The Gospels quote it at the Savior's triumphal entry.
concepts.ponder: What does the Savior's humility teach me about His kind of power?

concepts.title: Thirty pieces of silver and the One they pierced
concepts.text: Zechariah's later chapters contain details the New Testament ties to the Savior: thirty pieces of silver, a pierced one mourned like an only son, and wounds in His hands.
concepts.ponder: How do these prophecies deepen my gratitude for His sacrifice?

concepts.title: Holiness to the Lord on everything
concepts.text: On the last day the Mount of Olives splits, the Lord is king over all the earth, and even horses' bells and kitchen pots carry the words holiness unto the Lord.
concepts.ponder: What ordinary part of my day could I make holy to the Lord?

weeks.title: I Have Loved You, Saith the Lord
weeks.label: Malachi 1-4
weeks.overview: The last book of the Old Testament opens with the Lord saying simply, I have loved you. Malachi then challenges half-hearted offerings, promises a messenger and a refiner, opens the windows of heaven to the faithful, and closes with Elijah turning the hearts of fathers and children. The Savior quoted Malachi 3 and 4 to the Nephites (3 Nephi 24 and 25).

concepts.title: I have loved you
concepts.text: The book begins with the Lord's love, even as the people ask how He has shown it.
concepts.ponder: How has the Lord shown His love to me this year?

concepts.title: Offering the Lord my best
concepts.text: Priests brought blind and lame animals they would never give a governor. The Lord asks for wholehearted offerings.
concepts.ponder: Am I giving the Lord my leftovers or my best?

concepts.title: A messenger, and a Refiner's fire
concepts.text: The Lord will send a messenger to prepare His way and will come like a refiner's fire and fullers' soap, purifying His people.
concepts.ponder: What is the Lord refining in me?

concepts.title: Tithes and the windows of heaven
concepts.text: The people ask how they have robbed God. The answer is tithes and offerings, with a promise of blessings poured out with no room to hold them.
concepts.ponder: What blessings have come from paying an honest tithe?

concepts.title: A book of remembrance
concepts.text: Those who feared the Lord talked often together, and He wrote their names in a book of remembrance and called them His jewels.
concepts.ponder: Who do I talk with often about the Lord?

concepts.title: The Sun of righteousness with healing in His wings
concepts.text: For those who fear His name, the Savior rises like the sun with healing.
concepts.ponder: Where do I need His healing?

concepts.title: Elijah and turning hearts
concepts.text: Malachi promises Elijah will come before the great day to turn the hearts of fathers and children to each other. Moroni quoted it to Joseph Smith, and Elijah came in the Kirtland Temple.
concepts.ponder: Whose heart, living or gone before, is mine meant to turn toward?

weeks.title: We Have Waited for Him, and He Will Save Us
weeks.label: Christmas: Old Testament prophecies of Christ
weeks.overview: For Christmas, look back over the Old Testament as a long, hopeful wait for the Savior. Prophets foretold a virgin's son named Immanuel, a child called Wonderful Counsellor and Prince of Peace, a ruler from Bethlehem, a branch from Jesse, a shepherd for His flock and a man of sorrows who would carry our griefs. Isaiah sums up the wait: we have waited for Him, and He will save us.

concepts.title: We have waited for Him
concepts.text: Isaiah pictures the Lord swallowing up death and wiping away tears, and His people saying this is our God, we have waited for Him.
concepts.ponder: What am I waiting on the Lord for this Christmas?

concepts.title: Immanuel: God with us
concepts.text: A sign of a child whose name means God is with us. Matthew connects it with Mary and the Savior's birth.
concepts.ponder: When have I felt that God is with me?

concepts.title: Unto us a child is born
concepts.text: The child's names describe His work: Wonderful, Counsellor, the mighty God, the everlasting Father, the Prince of Peace.
concepts.ponder: Which of His names means the most to me right now, and why?

concepts.title: Out of Bethlehem
concepts.text: Micah named the small town where the ruler of Israel would come from.
concepts.ponder: What small and humble beginnings has the Lord used in my life?

concepts.title: A branch from the root of Jesse
concepts.text: From David's family line comes a ruler full of the Spirit who judges the poor with righteousness.
concepts.ponder: How does the Savior judge differently than the world does?

concepts.title: He shall feed His flock like a shepherd
concepts.text: A voice prepares His way, and the Lord comes gathering lambs in His arms.
concepts.ponder: When have I felt carried by the Good Shepherd?

concepts.title: A Star out of Jacob
concepts.text: Even Balaam, a foreign prophet, saw a Star coming out of Jacob.
concepts.ponder: How can I help others see His light?

concepts.title: A man of sorrows
concepts.text: The Christmas child came to carry our griefs and be wounded for our transgressions, so that by His stripes we are healed.
concepts.ponder: How does His Atonement change how I see Christmas?
